eyebrow: Declare the table, then fill it yourself
code:
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.ProductPriceHistory(@ProductID int)
RETURNS @Result TABLE
(
    ProductID int, ListPrice money, PriceTier varchar(10)
)
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO @Result (ProductID, ListPrice, PriceTier)
    SELECT ProductID, ListPrice,
           CASE WHEN ListPrice > 1000 THEN 'High'
                WHEN ListPrice > 100  THEN 'Mid'
                ELSE 'Low' END
    FROM Production.Product WHERE ProductID = @ProductID;
    RETURN;
END;
caption: RETURNS @Result TABLE (cols), then BEGIN/END fills it with INSERT.

eyebrow: Looks identical to an iTVF from the outside
caption: The difference is entirely inside the function, not in how you call it.

-- The optimizer can't see inside the BEGIN/END body.
-- It has to GUESS the row count an MSTVF returns --
-- historically a poor, fixed guess -- which can lead
-- to a bad join plan for everything downstream.
caption: An iTVF doesn't have this problem, because there's nothing to guess.
